keys.reason:
A whole agent run's usage, moved off gen_ai.usage.* by the TypeScript
SDK on producers known to repeat it on each call's span. Never read as
usage, so the run is not counted twice.

Copied, never summed with the cache counts: every bundled instrumentor
already reports it inclusive of them.

The conventions define no total: they record input and output and leave
the sum to the reader. The sink reads it for validation only.
A subset of the input count, never added to it.
A subset of the output count, never added to it.

Cost stays off the wire on purpose: the backend prices from the token
counts with its own table, so a producer's figure is never trusted.

The cache-write count's name before the conventions renamed it.
Current releases still send it (pydantic-ai, @ai-sdk/otel), and the
backend prices cache writes from the canonical key alone.
pydantic-ai's OpenAI reasoning split.
pydantic-ai's Anthropic reasoning split.
pydantic-ai's Google reasoning split.

pydantic-ai's backwards-compatible copy of the cache-read count, which
it also writes under the canonical key. The sink maps it only as a
fallback; the SDKs leave it, since the canonical key is always there.
As cache_read_tokens, for cache writes.

pydantic-ai's OpenAI output audio count: its chat adapter copies
completion_tokens_details whole, and its realtime adapter writes the
output audio under this name. The name carries no direction, and
pydantic-ai writes the same count as details.output_audio_tokens,
which is mapped, so this copy stays.

pydantic-ai's audio input count. A subset of the input count, never
added to it. On Gemini it is the audio prompt split plus the audio
tool-use prompt split, so it wins over details.audio_prompt_tokens.
OpenInference's and @ai-sdk/otel's audio input keys win over it.

pydantic-ai's cached audio input count. A subset of the cache-read
count, never added to it. Wins over details.audio_cache_tokens, which
carries the same count on Gemini.

pydantic-ai's audio output count. A subset of the output count, never
added to it. Wins over details.audio_candidates_tokens and
details.audio_response_tokens, which carry the same count on Gemini.
OpenInference's audio output key wins over it.

pydantic-ai's Google image input split (promptTokensDetails, modality
IMAGE). A subset of the input count, never added to it.

pydantic-ai's Google cached image split (cacheTokensDetails, modality
IMAGE). A subset of the cache-read count, never added to it.

pydantic-ai's Google image output split (candidatesTokensDetails,
modality IMAGE). A subset of the output count, never added to it.

pydantic-ai's Google audio input split (promptTokensDetails, modality
AUDIO). A subset of the input count, never added to it. A fallback for
details.input_audio_tokens, which wins.

pydantic-ai's Google cached audio split (cacheTokensDetails, modality
AUDIO). A subset of the cache-read count, never added to it. A fallback
for details.cache_audio_read_tokens, which wins.

pydantic-ai's Google audio output split (candidatesTokensDetails,
modality AUDIO). A subset of the output count, never added to it. A
fallback for details.output_audio_tokens, which wins.

The image part of Google's tool-use prompt, a second image input split
beside image_prompt_tokens. The image input key would be their sum, and
a normalizer renames a count, never adds two, so it stays.

The image output split on pydantic-ai's realtime path (the Gemini Live
API's responseTokensDetails). Live output is text or audio, so no image
count is expected there, and nothing reads one.

pydantic-ai's Google audio output split on its realtime path (the
Gemini Live API's responseTokensDetails, modality AUDIO). A subset of
the output count, never added to it. A fallback for
details.output_audio_tokens, which wins.

The audio part of Google's tool-use prompt, a second audio input split
beside audio_prompt_tokens. genai-prices already adds it into the
details.input_audio_tokens count that pydantic-ai writes, which is
mapped, and a normalizer renames a count, never adds two, so it stays.

The text subset of a transcription span's input, beside
input_token_details.audio_tokens. It belongs in
gen_ai.usage.text.input_tokens, but no normalizer maps it yet, so the
text split of the input is not attributed.

pydantic-ai's whole-run total on its agent span, next to each call's
usage on the call's own span. Reading it as usage would count the run
twice; it stays under its own name, which nothing reads.

pydantic-ai's own price for the call. Cost stays off the wire on
purpose, as with llm.cost.total.

pydantic-ai's prompt-cache health diagnostics (the cached prefix a
conversation established, hit ratio, misses), not provider usage.
OpenLLMetry's input count before the GenAI rename (0.47 and earlier).
OpenLLMetry's output count before the GenAI rename (0.47 and earlier).
OpenLLMetry's and Laminar's cache-read count (Anthropic's field name).
OpenLLMetry's and Laminar's cache-write count (Anthropic's field name).
OpenLLMetry's reasoning count.
OpenLLMetry's reasoning count in older releases.

Not a convention key: OpenLLMetry's total. No canonical key holds a
total, so it stays on the span as an extra.
OpenLLMetry's and Laminar's total, as gen_ai.usage.total_tokens.
Inclusive of the cached tokens, as the canonical key is.

v5's input count on generateText and generateObject, left unread on
purpose. On a model call the AI SDK writes the same value to
gen_ai.usage.input_tokens itself. On the generateText wrapper v5 takes
it from the LAST step's response, not the run's total (v5's streams and
v6 report the total under ai.usage.inputTokens), so mapping it to
rius.aggregated_usage.* would put a short total under a key that
promises the whole run.
An embedding call's input count (ai.embed, ai.embedMany and their doEmbed).
v5's output count on generateText and generateObject; as ai.usage.promptTokens.

v5's cache-read count, still written beside the detailed spelling by
v6. Without it cached input was priced as uncached.
v5's reasoning count, still written beside the detailed spelling by v6.

The uncached remainder of ai.usage.inputTokens. The conventions record
the inclusive input count and the cached part; this is their difference.

The non-reasoning remainder of ai.usage.outputTokens; the conventions
record the inclusive output count and the reasoning part.
A total; the conventions define none.

A request parameter, mapped to gen_ai.request.max_tokens (which the AI
SDK also writes itself on a model call).

@ai-sdk/otel's speech and transcription spans, with its usage option:
the provider's usage object whole, as a JSON string, in whatever units
the provider bills (tokens, seconds, characters). The integration also
writes its numeric leaves on the same span as gen_ai.usage.<key>, which
is what is read (input_tokens, output_tokens) or decided above, so
parsing this would count the same usage twice.
A throughput figure, not a count.

@arizeai/openinference-vercel's metadata.* mirror of
ai.response.avgOutputTokensPerSecond. No recording carries it: the
TypeScript SDK no longer runs that transform. An app can still run the
package's span processor itself on a provider the SDK bridges onto, and
its spans then carry the mirror, so the entry stays.
A request parameter (registry/model_parameters.yaml), not usage.
